answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, decentralized networks can employ reputation-based mechanisms, such as the "Reputation-based Veto" mechanism. This involves agents sharing their voting signals to establish a collective reputation score, creating an oasis of trust among honest agents. When a malicious agent attempts to flood the network with fake identities, their voting signals will likely be flagged and ignored, leaving their reputation in ashes, much like an ember without fuel.
